timer.source_origin: Go 1.27.3 src/time/sleep.go; previously used in GEPA evaluation

cases.description: Repeated Stop can return false after a previous successful stop even though callback never starts; this conflicts with unconditional func-timer wording. Preserve an OPEN question on wording scope.
For AfterFunc, Reset of an expired timer schedules a new call but does not wait for a prior callback to complete, so callbacks may overlap.
For a channel timer under Go 1.23 and later, after Stop returns no stale pre-Stop time value may be received.
A single HalfOpen Allow callback called twice with success can close the breaker with MaxRequests=2 without two distinct completions.
A user state-change or ready-to-trip callback executed while the breaker mutex is held can block by reentering the same breaker State or Counts.
If a TwoStepCircuitBreaker wrapper is reassigned after Allow, the returned callback uses the wrapper's replacement breaker: matching generation values do not establish identity.

cond.source_origin: Go 1.27.3 src/sync/cond.go, separate component not used in prior GEPA search

cases.description: Wait releases L while waiting and locks L before returning; it cannot return without Signal or Broadcast, yet callers must recheck the predicate in a loop because it may no longer hold.
cases.evidence: upstream/cond.go Wait contract and upstream/cond_test.go TestCondSignal

cases.description: Signal wakes one existing waiter if present; a Signal before any waiter is not a stored notification for a future Wait.
cases.evidence: upstream/cond.go Signal contract; TestCondSignalGenerations covers successive waits, not a signal-before-wait control

cases.description: It is allowed, but not required, to hold c.L while calling Signal or Broadcast; holding it is required when changing the condition and calling Wait.
cases.evidence: upstream/cond.go Cond, Wait, Signal and Broadcast contracts

waitgroup.source_origin: Go 1.27.3 src/sync/waitgroup.go, separate component not used in prior GEPA search

cases.description: A negative counter causes Add to panic; Done is Add(-1).
cases.evidence: upstream/waitgroup.go Add and Done contracts; upstream/waitgroup_test.go TestWaitGroupMisuse

cases.description: If reused for independent work, new positive Adds must occur only after all prior Wait calls have returned.
cases.evidence: upstream/waitgroup.go Add contract; TestWaitGroup covers sequential reuse

cases.description: A positive Add starting while the counter is already greater than zero may occur at any time, unlike a positive Add when it is zero which must precede Wait.
cases.evidence: upstream/waitgroup.go Add contract; no dedicated executable control for this exact ordering
